description: Long-term energy conservation is the gold standard for validating gravitational integrators. An energy drift monitor tracks the relative energy error |E(t) - E(0)| / |E(0)| over time, distinguishing between bounded oscillation (symplectic integrators), linear drift (non-symplectic), and random walk (optimal per Brouwer's law). This serves as both a diagnostic and a stopping criterion.
mathematical_formalization: E(t) = T(t) + V(t) = (1/2) sum_i m_i |v_i|^2 + sum_{i<j} -G*m_i*m_j/|r_i - r_j|. Relative error: delta_E(t) = |E(t) - E(0)| / |E(0)|. For symplectic: delta_E ~ O(dt^p) bounded. For Brouwer's law: delta_E ~ sqrt(t) * O(dt^p).
analogical_connections: Financial auditing: tracking cumulative errors in accounts
Signal integrity in communications: bit error rate monitoring
Climate model validation: tracking global energy balance
implementation_hypothesis: Compute E_kinetic and E_potential each step. Store time series of delta_E. Fit log-log slope to classify drift type.
experiment_seed: Run same initial conditions with Euler, RK4, leapfrog, Verlet for 10^6 steps. Plot delta_E(t) on log-log axes.
